lessons.title: Sounds & identity
lessons.objective: Introduce yourself simply.
lessons.cultural_notes: Yoruba is tonal — listen before perfection.

vocab.example: Mo ń kọ́ èdè Yorùbá — I am learning Yoruba. Builds rapport with native speakers.
Orúkọ mi ni — My name is…. Introduce yourself before requests.
Ó dára — It is good / fine. Positive response in conversation.

grammar: Pattern: subject → verb → object (default sentence order).
Listen for the verb stem; affixes carry tense and person.

lessons.title: Morning greetings
lessons.objective: Greet by time of day.
lessons.cultural_notes: Greeting culture is the spine of social life.

vocab.example: Ẹ kú àárọ̀ — Good morning (to elders/group). Time-based greeting; always greet before asking for anything.
Báwo ni — How are you? (informal). Casual; use with peers.
Mo ń ṣe dáadáa — I am fine. Standard reply to báwo ni.

grammar: Pattern: greeting → reply → follow-up question.
Always greet before asking anything else.
Use the polite/elder form when in doubt.
